title: Marguerite and the Drop
premise: Xanthe Coldharbour, a disgraced intelligence analyst living off-grid in Lisbon, is summoned by a former handler to verify a single anomaly: passenger flight 447's digital footprint is being erased in real time while the plane is still airborne. As he digs, he discovers the erasure is cover for a staged mid-air 'accident' meant to kill a whistleblower carrying evidence of a sanctioned assassination program. Burned by every institution that once employed him, Xanthe assembles a crew of fellow castoffs — a forger, an air-traffic insider, and Marguerite, the whistleblower's estranged daughter — to expose the plot and stop the attack before the extraction flight leaves at dawn. In the end, they force the plane down at a closed military strip, broadcast the evidence, and Xanthe chooses truth over the loyalty that burned him, walking away with a found family instead of a badge.
about_author: Rafael Voss is the pen name of a former aviation logistics consultant who spent a decade inside the paperwork of international charter flights. He writes thrillers about the people systems discard, from a farmhouse outside Porto.

chapters.title: The Go-Bag by the Door
chapters.summary: POV: Xanthe. Living quietly in Lisbon under a polished alias, Xanthe is haunted by his dismissal from three agencies and keeps a packed bag as ritual. A coded message from his old handler, Odile, breaks the routine: 'Verify 447.' The beat is uneasy calm — a man who expects exile to end badly.

chapters.title: A Flight That Isn't There
chapters.summary: POV: Xanthe. Cross-checking databases, Xanthe watches flight 447's records dissolve — manifests, transponder logs, even the airline's own booking history — while radar shows it still climbing over the Atlantic. His handler goes silent. The beat is vertigo: the machinery of truth itself is being rewritten.

chapters.title: Marguerite
chapters.summary: POV: Marguerite. In Marseille, Marguerite Delacroix learns her estranged father — a flight-safety auditor — boarded 447 carrying a drive that could topple an assassination program. Men she doesn't know ransack his flat. She flees with a duplicate key to his safe-deposit box. The beat is grief weaponized into purpose.

chapters.title: Three Burned Strangers
chapters.summary: POV: Xanthe. Xanthe tracks the erasure to a private contractor and realizes he can't work alone; he recruits Tomas, a forger he once betrayed, and Nia, a grounded air-traffic controller. Their first joint move recovers the deposit-box key's location. The beat is brittle trust among people trained to lie.

chapters.title: What Was in the Hold
chapters.summary: POV: Marguerite. Opening the safe-deposit box, Marguerite finds not the drive but her father's flight manifest annotated with a cargo code — and a photo of Xanthe's name on an old kill-list review board. She confronts him in Lisbon. The beat is betrayal: the ally may be the enemy.

chapters.title: The Dawn Window
chapters.summary: POV: Xanthe. Decoding the manifest, the team learns the plan: 447 will be downed over open water and blamed on a maintenance failure, timed so an extraction flight leaves a private strip at dawn — carrying the program's architects to immunity. Xanthe confesses his past complicity to Marguerite. The beat is shame converted into resolve.

chapters.title: Static Over the Atlantic
chapters.summary: POV: Nia. From a hijacked control position, Nia feeds the team live tracking while the contractor's operatives close in. Tomas forges credentials to get them onto the private strip; Marguerite deciphers her father's final message hidden in the manifest margins. The beat is the clock tightening — hours, not days.

chapters.title: Guns at the Fence
chapters.summary: POV: Xanthe. Infiltrating the strip, the team is spotted; Tomas is captured covering their retreat, and Odile reappears — revealed as the contractor's architect, offering Xanthe redemption if he stands down. He refuses. The beat is loyalty tested and found hollow against truth.

chapters.title: Forty Minutes to Dawn
chapters.summary: POV: Marguerite. Racing the extraction flight, Marguerite and Xanthe reach the tower and force 447 to divert using Nia's forged emergency directives, while broadcasting the drive's contents to press contacts worldwide. Odile orders the strike anyway; the crew must physically hold the tower. The beat is white-knuckle climax.

chapters.title: Landing Light
chapters.summary: POV: Xanthe. 447 lands at dawn as the evidence floods every feed; Odile is arrested by her own security detail flipping sides, and Tomas walks free in the chaos. Xanthe burns his last alias, keeping only the go-bag — now packed for a life chosen, not fled. The beat is quiet justice and earned belonging.
